section_summary: This section reports a perceived decline in the Japan Communist Party’s electoral and labor strength during 1949, while cautioning that the party could adapt. It also covers Communist-linked efforts to promote Soviet-Japanese trade and reopen northern fisheries, Sino-Japanese friendship activities, and a petition to send delegates to an Asiatic Women’s Conference.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of “Japan Communist Party Comparative Political Strength”
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a military intelligence assessment of the Japan Communist Party’s political strength.
subfiles.summary: Reports recent Communist losses in labor and rural politics, while warning that the party may adapt.

subfiles.title: JCP Comparative Political Strength
subfiles.about: Assesses Communist membership, labor influence, election results, and relations with Social Democrats.
subfiles.summary: The report estimates Communist members and active sympathizers and describes declining influence in the railway and communications unions. It compares the party’s January general-election gains with weak subsequent agrarian and local election results. It also describes Social Democratic resistance to cooperation and concludes that the party is on the defensive, though capable of adjusting its tactics.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo’s despatch 844
subfiles.about: Summarizes the intelligence report’s assessment of Communist setbacks.
subfiles.summary: Notes Communist losses in union leadership and elections, alongside the party’s capacity to recover.

subfiles.title: Sino-Japanese friendship and Communist activities
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Communist-linked Sino-Japanese friendship activities and advocacy of trade with China.
subfiles.summary: Describes a Tokyo meeting praising China’s new government and a friendship society’s campaign for trade with Communist China.

subfiles.title: Communist Policy Toward the Northern Fishery Problem
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Explains Communist use of the northern fisheries issue to promote Soviet ties and win fishermen’s support.
subfiles.summary: Sebald describes the Japan-Soviet Friendship Society’s trade campaign and Communist proposals for reopening northern fisheries or forming cooperative fishing ventures with the Soviet Union and Communist China. He argues that restricted fishing grounds make these appeals potentially attractive to Japanese fishermen.

subfiles.title: Trade Policies of the Japan-Soviet Friendship Society
subfiles.from: Military Intelligence Section, Far East Command
subfiles.about: Examines the society’s leadership, trade promotion, Communist ties, and northern fisheries campaign.
subfiles.summary: The report traces the society’s founding, Soviet sponsorship, Communist-linked officers, and efforts to attract unions and small industrialists through prospects for Soviet trade. It recounts meetings advocating shipbuilding orders and expanded fishing rights. It concludes that the society provides a channel for Communist and Soviet economic and political messages.

subfiles.title: “Seek Reopening of Northern Sea Fishing Through Soviet-Japanese Friendship”
subfiles.about: Reports a conference urging a nationwide campaign to reopen northern fisheries.
subfiles.summary: Participants propose cooperation among fishermen, employers, and political groups to secure access to northern waters through Soviet-Japanese friendship.

subfiles.title: “Importance of Restored Fishing Industry Stressed”
subfiles.about: Presents Tokuda Kyūichi’s Communist Party policy speech on restoring Japan’s fishing industry.
subfiles.summary: Tokuda links restricted fishing grounds to the industry’s decline and proposes cooperation with the Soviet Union and Communist China. He also advocates changes to finance, taxation, industry management, and oceanographic research.

subfiles.title: Asiatic Women’s Conference
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a petition concerning Japanese participation in the Asiatic Women’s Conference.
subfiles.summary: Reports the selection of nine Japanese and one Korean prospective delegate and the absence of travel clearance.

subfiles.title: Petition for participation in the Asiatic Women’s Conference
subfiles.from: Preparatory Committee for Participation in Asiatic Women’s Conference in Japan
subfiles.about: Requests help sending a Japanese women’s delegation to the conference in Beijing.
subfiles.summary: Describes the delegate-selection campaign and asks Sebald to enable the delegation’s participation.

subfiles.title: List of Japanese Delegation to Asiatic Women’s Conference
subfiles.from: Preparatory Committee for Participation in Asiatic Women’s Conference in Japan
subfiles.about: Lists prospective delegates and their affiliations.
subfiles.summary: Names prospective delegates from women’s groups, unions, and Korean women’s organizations in Japan.

subfiles.title: Affiliates of the Preparatory Committee for Participation in Asiatic Women’s Conference
subfiles.from: Preparatory Committee for Participation in Asiatic Women’s Conference in Japan
subfiles.about: Lists unions and women’s organizations affiliated with the preparatory committee.
subfiles.summary: Identifies labor, political, cooperative, and women’s groups affiliated with the conference preparatory committee.
